The `summary()` function reports the minimum, quartiles, mean, maximum,
and number of missing values in one call;
its quartiles use R's default interpolating quantile rule (`type = 7`),
so they can differ slightly from @def-quartiles:

```{r}
#| label: summary-chol
summary(wcgs$chol)
```

For a formatted table of several variables at once,
`gtsummary::tbl_summary()` is useful (@tbl-wcgs-summary-continuous).

::: {#tbl-wcgs-summary-continuous}

```{r}
wcgs |>
  dplyr::select(age, chol, sbp, dbp, bmi, weight) |>
  gtsummary::tbl_summary(
    statistic = list(
      gtsummary::all_continuous() ~
        "{mean} ({sd}); {median} [{p25}, {p75}]"
    ),
    digits = gtsummary::all_continuous() ~ 1
  )
```

WCGS: descriptive statistics for continuous variables

:::
